extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of modern European history
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for composing interpretive, contextual histories of events such as the French Revolution and Napoleonic era; emphasizes balancing perspective, economic and institutional analysis, and character study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exaggerating the Terror; present its real dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is well to remind the reader here of the real dimensions of this phase of the Terror, which strikes so vividly upon the imagination and which has therefore been enormously exaggerated relatively to the rest of the revolution."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast vivid, sensational episodes with broader quantitative and contextual evidence (e.g., total condemned ~ a few thousands), and resist letting striking imagery determine the overall judgment of a period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance attention to notable victims with broader social context
rubrics_metrics.description: "We hear so much about the martyrs of the French Terror because they were notable, well-connected people, and because there has been a sort of propaganda of their sufferings. But let us balance against them in our minds what was going on in the prisons of the world generally at that time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare high-profile cases with contemporaneous practices elsewhere (examples given: hangings in Massachusetts, prison conditions in Britain and America, Howard's findings) to avoid a one-sided narrative that privileges elites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize revolutionary ideas beyond individual caricatures
rubrics_metrics.description: "It witnesses to the immense vitality ... that it could still flow in a creative torrent after it had been caricatured and mocked in the grotesque personality and career of Robespierre.... the power of these ideas was not destroyed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that the force of political ideas can outlive and transcend the failings or excesses of particular leaders; avoid reducing movements to single personalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure history around core socio-economic problems (Property, Currency, International Relationship)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The New Order found itself confronted with three riddles which it was quite unprepared to solve: Property, Currency, and International Relationship."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear organizing problems or 'riddles' to frame narrative and analysis; take them in turn and explain how each shaped political choices and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain complex economic phenomena in practical, everyday terms
rubrics_metrics.description: "However complicated the origins of currency, its practical effect and the end it has to serve in the community may be stated roughly in simple terms. The money a man receives for his work ... must ultimately be able to purchase for him a fairly equivalent amount of consumable goods."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate abstract monetary issues into concrete effects on wages, prices, and daily life (use seasonal examples, wartime destruction, and buying-power illustrations) so readers grasp stakes and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize the imperative premise before technical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: "The imperative need for that steadfastness and security of currency is the fixed datum from which the scientific study and control of currency must begin."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the fundamental assumptions or fixed datums (what counts as a 'healthy' currency, etc.) before engaging in technical or policy critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative data and analogies to calibrate scale and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: "More lives were wasted by the British generals alone on the opening day of what is known as the Somme offensive of July, 1916, than in the whole French revolution from start to finish."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ cross-period or cross-national comparisons and vivid analogies to help readers judge relative importance and avoid sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze continuities and contradictions between ideals and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: "So within ten years of the meeting of the States General, New France begins to take on a singular likeness to the old ... it has a new army--but a damaged fleet; it has new rich people instead of the old rich people ... a new foreign policy curiously like the old foreign policy disrobed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight where revolutionary rhetoric and promised changes revert to older patterns (e.g., exploitation of conquered lands); critique hypocrisy and trace institutional continuities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine personalities in the light of mixed motives; avoid simplistic hagiography or demonization
rubrics_metrics.description: "...one of the most illuminating figures in modern history, the figure of an adventurer and a wrecker, whose story seems to display ... the universal subtle conflict of egotism, vanity, and personality with the weaker, wider claims of the common good."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present leaders as complex actors with competing motives (ambition, vanity, idealism); use biographical detail and quoted passages to illustrate internal contradictions rather than reduce characters to pure villainy or heroism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace long-term intellectual and moral developments to situate present debates
rubrics_metrics.description: "A steady, continuous criticism of the permissible scope of property seems to have been going on in the world for the last twenty-five or thirty centuries."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place contemporary arguments and policies within longue durée intellectual and moral histories to show continuities, shifts, and inherited assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and call out propaganda or partisan distortions
rubrics_metrics.description: "...there has been a sort of propaganda of their sufferings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to propagandistic narratives that amplify particular perspectives; explicitly name and correct distortions by supplying alternative evidence and context.
